Filing gate: ③ a skills-doc follow-up owed by a narrowing PR: PR #27584 (#27457) makes the console read a bare-string predicate as CEL, the way `@objectstack/spec` defines it and the server already reads it. Its PR body carries `Skills-docs: follow-up #<this card>`.
Business reason: AI agents learn predicate syntax from `skills/objectui`. Those files teach the legacy JavaScript grammar (`===`, the JS operator table, raw JS conditions), which the server already refuses and which the console will fault on once #27584 lands. An agent following the skill writes a `hidden` / `visibleWhen` that silently hides or never shows the element.
Reader who acts: the triage seat, then the lane that owns `skills/**` (per `execution-duties.md`, a `skills/**` change runs at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, no one-line exemption, which is why it is not done inside #27584's default-tier card thread).
Timing: should land with or right after #27584; until then the skill and the runtime disagree.

## Lines found by #27584's card thread (on `origin/main`)

- `skills/objectui/rules/protocol.md:17`: `"hidden": "data.status === 'draft'"`.
- `skills/objectui/guides/schema-expressions.md`: line 10 (`data.status === 'active'` as the condition example); lines 83–89 (the operator table counts JS operators as condition syntax); line 254; lines 335–336.

## Expected

Each bare-predicate example is CEL (`==`, `!`, `in`, `size()`, …); the operator table states that a bare condition string is CEL and that `${…}` templates keep their own grammar; a short FROM → TO list for the common JS spellings (`===`/`!==`, `.includes`, `.length`, a missing `data.*` key) sits in the guide, since the #27584 changeset carries `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` (no protocol-legal metadata needs rewriting).
